item.title: People's houses are collapsing into the ocean. FEMA gives them no other option
item.description: Waterfront homes are collapsing along the coast. Homeowners generally have plenty of warning before their house buckles. So why aren't most houses removed, or at least emptied, before they fall?
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Here's why an Arizona medical examiner is working to track heat-related deaths
item.description: No one across the U.S. is consistently tracking climate-fueled deaths. One medical examiner has a new protocol on heat-deaths.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: In Florida, textbook publishers are minimizing or removing climate change coverage
item.description: The words "climate change" are slowly being removed from textbooks in Florida and from the state's education standards.
item.content:encoded: The words "climate change" are slowly being removed from textbooks in Florida and from the state's education standards.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Meszaros

item.title: Trump's EPA repeals pollution limits on fossil fuel power plants
item.description: The Trump administration is eliminating limits on climate-warming pollution from the nation's fossil fuel power plants. Environmental groups say this will impact the climate and public health.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The Rio Grande is having its driest year on record
item.description: Colorado River drought gets a lot of headlines, but the Rio Grande is having one of its driest years ever. What a recent surge of water for nature says about its future.
item.content:encoded: Colorado River drought gets a lot of headlines, but the Rio Grande is having one of its driest years ever. What a recent surge of water for nature says about its future.

item.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
item.description: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A new report finds many Chinese provinces are reducing their use of coal
item.description: China is the world's largest emitter of planet-warming pollution. But a new report this week finds the country is transitioning away from fossil fuels including coal.

item.title: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
item.description: Heat kills thousands of people across the U.S. every year. The risk is especially high for the millions of Americans who live in manufactured housing like mobile homes and trailers.

item.title: Forecasters sound the alarm over a powerful El Nino climate pattern
item.description: Forecasters expect the El Niño weather pattern to strengthen significantly this year, raising the risks of extreme weather around the world well into 2027.
